title: A Hospital within a Monastery: An Examination of Medical Remains at the Alahana Parivena Monastery in Polonnaruva, Sri Lanka
author_or_institution: Saman Nanayakkara, M. S. Gunarathna, Aruna Rajapaksa, D. Thusitha Mendis, D. K. Jayarathne and Aravindi Abeyrathne / SAARC Journal of Social Science
author_institution: University of Peradeniya; Rajarata University of Sri Lanka
scope: Alahana Parivena excavation history, monastic hospital architecture, medicinal trough, sanitary complex, surgical and medical artefacts, and the parivena as an organised educational institution
limitations: The accessible copy is an author-uploaded version of the 2026 SAARC Journal article. Functional interpretation of individual instruments remains partly inferential, although the hospital context and assemblage are archaeologically anchored.

title: Surgical Instruments at the Alahana Parivena Hospital in Polonnaruwa
author_or_institution: Arjuna Aluwihare / Journal of History, Art and Archaeology
scope: Clinical and functional assessment of excavated instruments from the Alahana Parivena hospital assemblage
limitations: The article is written from a surgical-history perspective and some specific uses are inferred by analogy with modern instruments; use it together with excavation-context sources rather than as a sole archaeological anchor.

title: Analysis of Historical Trends and Recent Elimination of Malaria from Sri Lanka and Its Applicability for Malaria Control in Other Countries
author_or_institution: Dilrukshi A. Wijesundere and Ranjan Ramasamy / Frontiers in Public Health
scope: Historical malaria ecology in Sri Lanka, retrospective association of malaria-like disease with thirteenth-century Polonnaruwa, and irrigation/vector plausibility
limitations: This is a retrospective epidemiological reconstruction. It makes a biologically plausible association but does not provide palaeopathological or demographic proof that malaria caused Polonnaruwa's political collapse.

title: Our history
scope: Oxford teaching attested in 1096 and institutional development during the twelfth and early thirteenth centuries
limitations: Institutional self-history, appropriate for Oxford chronology but not for comparative claims about Sri Lankan monastic institutions.

title: Sīhaḷa Saṅgha and Laṅkā in Later Premodern Southeast Asia
author_or_institution: Anne M. Blackburn / Cambridge University Press
scope: Second-millennium mobility of monks, ordination lineages, educational practices, texts and linguistic preferences between Lanka and mainland Southeast Asia
limitations: The author explicitly cautions that the transregional history is incompletely reconstructed; use as evidence for networks and mobility, not a one-way Sri Lankan civilisational export model.

title: Polonnaruwa
scope: Official heritage synthesis of Polonnaruwa, Alahana Parivena as a major monastic educational complex, Buddhist/Hindu monuments and the post-thirteenth-century decline of the city
limitations: Public heritage synthesis; the phrase 'monastic university' is interpretive and must not be transported into a claim of institutional equivalence with European universities.
